The paper reports different erasure estimates from tomography and randomized benchmarking. Those are distinct from an unconditional gate-fidelity claim.

The finite-pulse comparison initially looked favorable, but it contained two errors: omitted phase accumulation during SWS swaps and an incorrect physical rail assignment. After correcting both and independently replaying the fixed calculations:

Declared leading-loss comparison	Ideal piecewise SWS	Best tested finite positive hump
Duration	0.449329 µs	0.668941 µs
Mean leading independent-loss dose	0.438486%	0.522443%

The tested hump is 19.15% worse in average loss, despite lower mediator participation. Its longer duration costs more cavity storage. The corrected source and review are 
ROOT_MEDIATOR_EXPOSURE_REVIEW.md

That is a negative result for the tested family and parameters, not a general optimal-control impossibility theorem. The conditional exposure bound also does not automatically apply to the many-oscillator cosine gate.
